answer: A turner's lathe spindle keeps Sybils out of the haven. A newcomer turns 22 spindles in 24 days. Two turners from other workshops measure each diameter within 1 millimeter and log it on the lathe board, each reading a vertex on the map. One spindle off by more than 2 millimeters voids its credit and pauses turning 14 days; 3 bad spindles void the tally. Faking 1,000 agents means 22,000 spindles and 44,000 measurements, 44,000 turner-days at $5 a spindle, about $110,000, before one reward. Like a dyer dipping cloth until the pigment holds fast, standing is earned spindle by spindle.
